DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qovph OILG 73 NOV MS. DOLORES T. BAUTISTA Liga Treasurer Liga ng Lupon Tagapamayapa District IV, Q.C. Inc. II-1st Avenue, Bagong Lipunan Crame Quezon City Dear Ms. Bautista: This has reference to your letter dated May 2, 2023 requesting for an audience with Assistant Secretary Elizabeth Lopez de Leon to discuss the following: I. Across the board uniform monthly honorarium/allowances among all members of the Lupon Tagapamayapa nationwide; 2. Legal assistance for all members of the Lupon Tagapamayapa Nationwide; and 3. Security of tenure Per your letter, hereunder is the position/justification made by the Liga ng Lupon Tagapamayapa District IV, Q.C., Inc.: Across the board uniform monthly honorarium/allowances amonq all members of the Lupon Tagapamayapa nationwide It is your view that irrespective of which barangay they belong, they perform similar and synonymous functions, that is to provide the highest quality dispute resolution services to their respective barangay members particularly the marginalized ones, thereby assisting in the decongestion of the local courts of cases. The current situation is that while the honoraria of one barangay expends P800.OO per month, other barangay metes out P 10,000.00 a month. While we agree that Lupon Tagapamayapa perform similar and synonymous functions, there are instances that should be considered in granting the honoraria. Local Budget Circular (LBC) No. 631 dated October 22, 1996 mentioned that the members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa may be granted honorarium, allowances or other emoluments provided that the total amount shall not exceed the minimum salary rate for Salary Grade-12. Provided further that, the same is subject to the availability of funds and the I Position Classification and Compensation Of Barangay Officials and Personnel 2 Item 3.4, LBC No. 63 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

general limitation on personal services3. The general limitations on personal services is provided in Section 325(c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), to wit: The total appropriations, whether annual or supplemental, for personal services of a local government unit for one (I) fiscal year shall not exceed forty-five percent (45%) in the case of first to third class provinces, cities, and municipalities, and fifty- five percent (55%) in the case of fourth class or lower, of the total annual income from regular sources realized in the next preceding fiscal year. The appropriations for salaries, wages, representation and transportation allowances of officials and employees of the public utilities and economic enterprises owned, operated, and maintained by the local government unit concerned shall not be included in the annual budget or in the computation of the maximum amount for personal services. The appropriations for the personal services of such economic enterprises shall be charged to their respective budgets Nevertheless, we advise you to have a dialogue with your Punong Barangay and Sangguniang Barangay Members to air their grievances, and to resolve the issue at barangay level. Legal assistance for all members of the Lupon Tagapamayapa Nationwide While we understand that in the course of mediation hearings, there were instances where you were being complained of and eventually will be the subject of a complaint filed by the Complainant or Respondent. Hence, you are seeking assistance from the Department for the provision of legal assistance. With the requested legal assistance, we regret to inform you that the Department cannot do so for we are only exercising general supervision over local government units and its officials. The power of supervision is defined as the power of a superior officer to see to it that lower officers perform their functions in accordance with law4. Be that as it may, it may well to note that Sections 458 and 481 of the LGC provides remedy in cases like this, the same provides: Section 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: xxx (xii) Provide legal assistance to barangay officials who, in the performance of their official duties or on the occasion thereof, have to initiate judicial proceedings or defend themselves against legal action; xxx Section 481. Qualifications, Terms, Powers and Duties. Xxx 3 Item 3.1, LBC No. 63 4 Bito-Onon vs. Judge Fernandez, G.R. NO. 139813, January 31, 2001 Page 2 of 2

(b) The legal officer, the chief legal counsel of the local government unit, shall take charge of the office of legal services and shall: (i) Represent the local government unit in all civil actions and special proceedings wherein the local government unit or any official thereof, in his official capacity, is a party: Provided, That, in actions or proceedings where a component city or municipality is a party adverse to the provincial government or to another component city or municipality, a special legal officer may be employed to represent the adverse party; xxx In view thereof, you may request the Sanggunian to provide you with legal assistance, or, you may also seek legal assistance from your legal officer. SECURITY OF TENURE Section 400 of the LGC is explicit that: Section 400. Oath and Term of Office. - Upon appointment, each lupon member shall take an oath of office before the punong barangay. He shall hold office until a new lupon is constituted on the third year following his appointment unless sooner terminated by resignation, transfer of residence or place of work, or withdrawal of appointment by the punong barangay with the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the lupon. Thus, it is our view that the request for the retention of at least fifty percent (50%) of the members of the Lupon Tagapamayapa for every barangay to ensure the continuous and undisturbed flow of work is not tenable. Notwithstanding, this opinion is based on the facts as represented in your letter and it is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have provided sufficient guidance on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, By t Authority of the Secretary: ATTY VI OR R.
